name: Roller skate or inline skate
blurb: Skating is a balance and edge skill. The order that works is: stand, fall safely, stop, then move — and almost everyone does it in the wrong order.
gear: Smooth flat ground away from traffic
steps: Learn to stand and balance on carpet or grass first, feet in a V, knees bent, weight forward over the balls of your feet.
Learn to fall safely — forwards onto knee pads then wrist guards, never backwards — before you can build any speed.
Learn to stop before you learn to go: the heel brake on inlines, or the T-stop and plough stop on quads.
Learn the duck walk on flat ground, then let it become a glide, pushing out to the side rather than backwards.
Learn to swizzle and to skate in a straight line with long, even strokes.
Add turning by leaning, and crossovers once the basics are secure.
tips: Standing upright is what causes backward falls, which are the ones that hurt your head. Stay bent and forward.
Not being able to stop is the reason beginners panic. Get the brake sorted first.
proof: You skate 500 metres confidently, turn both ways, and stop on command from speed.
